text:
Donald Trump and Dana White walked to the cage together before the UFC's White House event(Image: Paramount Plus)

The UFC’s White House event kicked off with a long entrance by Donald Trump and Dana White from the Oval Office to the cage on the South Lawn, including a somewhat awkward moment between the two.

The first-of-its-kind event on the grass in front of the presidential residence got off to a rocky start as poor weather in the area forced a delay in coverage. Around 8:30 p.m., Trump and White made their entrance to help officially start the evening.

But one moment in particular caught the attention of some viewers as Trump appeared to grab hold of the UFC president.

As the pair made its way toward the cage following a performance of the national anthem and a military flyover, Trump appeared to struggle walking in a straight line, grabbing White’s shoulder. It was unclear if he was using White to steady himself or simply pulling the UFC boss closer in a friendly manner.

“Trump looked like he almost just fell over into Dana #UFCWhiteHouse,” one user posted on X.

A look at the UFC's temporary structure on the White House's South Lawn

“Is it me or did Trump not look right during that walk out?” another asked.

“Trump looked gassed after that walk out,” a third user added.

Trump has sparked health fears at various times during his presidency. As recently as this week, Trump left viewers confused by claiming during a live television broadcast that a newly renovated swimming pool will be "taller than skyscrapers."

During an Oval Office meeting, the commander-in-chief declared the restored Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is "taller than any building in the world, actually".

He continued: "There's no building that's 2500 feet tall, I don't think. But it's twice as tall as the Empire State Building, and much wider. We just got that open last night. We wanted to do it before July 4, and it is incredible."

Trump also has appeared to struggle staying awake during several public appearances. Last week, he seemed to fall asleep for a significant period of time while attending Game 3 of the NBA Finals, not long after hearing a chorus of boos from the Madison Square Garden crowd.
